sections.heading: What the purchaser is buying

proposedPublicPatch.title: Who remains responsible for safety at a customer site?
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Employer safety duties at customer premises
proposedPublicPatch.description: A customer induction or a brand manual does not establish that the employer has met its safety duties.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: Working at someone else’s premises does not make safety only the customer’s problem. The actual employer, task and control of the work matter.

sections.heading: The employer duty is more than a contract clause
paragraphs: OSH Act section 5(a) requires a covered employer to provide a workplace free of recognised hazards causing or likely to cause death or serious physical harm, and to comply with applicable occupational safety and health standards.

A clause saying the local operator handles safety does not demonstrate that equipment, training and hazards have been addressed. Equally, the brand being overseas does not by itself decide its legal responsibility.

sections.heading: Law, customer rules and brand standards are different
paragraphs: A customer’s induction, insurance certificate and site rules can be part of the job arrangements. They do not establish compliance with every applicable standard. Identify the actual chemicals, equipment, access conditions and task hazards, and the federal OSHA or state-plan authority involved.

In a fictional case, a brand gives remote training before its partner’s employees service powered machinery at a customer site. If the general-industry hazardous-energy standard applies, the employer needs the required energy-control programme, procedures, training and inspections; a customer induction alone does not do that. Its scope and exceptions matter: for example, its cord-and-plug exception requires unplugging to control the hazard and the plug to remain under the servicing employee’s exclusive control.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Establish the actual job’s equipment, training and safety requirements before relying on a customer induction or general brand course.
limitations: This is an employer-duty baseline, not a task-specific OSHA or state-plan controls guide. It supplies no incident deadline or joint-employer determination.

proposedPublicPatch.title: Form I-9: completion and retention deadlines
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Form I-9 completion deadlines and retention dates
proposedPublicPatch.description: Know the employee and employer deadlines, including the shorter-employment exception and the later retention date.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: The hiring employer needs an I-9 process even if its owner stays overseas. This page explains federal completion and retention deadlines; the current USCIS form edition and detailed examination instructions were not verified in the recorded review.

sections.heading: Employee and employer steps have different deadlines
paragraphs: Form I-9 records employment eligibility verification. Under the cited regulation, the employee completes Section 1 at hire. The employer generally examines the required acceptable evidence and completes Section 2 within three business days of hire.

If employment lasts less than three business days, the employer’s examination and completion take place at hire instead, and a receipt cannot replace the required document. The regulation permits the employer, its agent or someone acting in its interest to perform the employer step. Arrange who will do it before work starts; ownership overseas does not change the deadlines or authorise an informal remote check.

sections.heading: A deadline does not establish a permitted checking method
paragraphs: The regulation recognises physical examination or an alternative procedure authorised under its specified conditions. A video call, emailed scan or overseas manager’s review is not automatically an authorised method. Use the official instructions to establish the applicable examination process before relying on it.

sections.heading: Keep the later of two retention dates
paragraphs: Retain the I-9 for three years after hire or one year after termination, whichever is later.

In a fictional example, an employee starts on January 15, 2027 and leaves on January 15, 2030. Three years after hire is January 15, 2030; one year after departure is January 15, 2031. The later date, January 15, 2031, controls this I-9 calculation. Other record-retention duties are separate.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Arrange a compliant examination process before the hire, and calculate both retention dates when employment ends.
limitations: This page does not determine individual work authorisation, E-Verify, anti-discrimination or visa-category questions.

proposedPublicPatch.title: A contractor label does not decide the technician’s status
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Worker classification: actual work and federal-source limits
proposedPublicPatch.description: Equipment ownership and a signed contractor clause are not a complete employment test.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: Look at how the person actually earns money and works. Different wage, tax and state tests can apply. The Department of Labor’s opinion-letter numbering is now reconciled, but this review does not establish the latest appellate status or classify your worker.

sections.heading: Is the person operating an independent business?
paragraphs: Relevant facts include who sets prices and schedules, accepts jobs, hires helpers, makes entrepreneurial investments, markets to other customers and has a genuine opportunity for profit or loss. Include actual practice and reserved rights.

In a fictional maintenance arrangement, the brand sets mandatory schedules and prices while the technician buys equipment. The contract says independent contractor, but says little about outside customers, helpers or profit and loss. Neither the label nor that purchase answers the whole question. Specialised skill alone does not establish an independent business.

sections.heading: The tax and wage questions are separate
paragraphs: The codified 29 CFR Part 795 interpretation reviewed in November 2026 examines the whole activity through six nonexclusive factors. No one factor or selected subset necessarily controls; it is not a points tally or a replacement for governing court law.

IRS employment-tax guidance instead groups common-law evidence into behavioural control, financial control and the type of relationship. It also considers the whole relationship; a right to control can matter even for remote work. A tax result or relief provision does not decide federal wage-and-hour duties under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) or state unemployment and wage law.

sections.heading: An investigation policy is not a repeal
paragraphs: The Department of Labor’s May 2025 bulletin changes its investigation approach within its stated scope and discretion; it expressly does not change employee rights or employer responsibilities. The named 2019 opinion was withdrawn in 2021 and expressly reissued, with its text reproduced, as FLSA2025-2 on May 2, 2025. That opinion concerns supplied virtual-marketplace facts, not automatic contractor treatment for technicians. The February 2026 replacement proposal, including its proposed expansion to the Family and Medical Leave Act and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act, is not effective merely because comments closed.

The cited Colt & Joe Trucking order concerned standing and stated alternative failed or waived arguments; it did not classify every technician. These source types cannot be used interchangeably to declare contractor treatment available.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Check the real control and independent-business facts before relying on contractor treatment in your staffing cost.
limitations: No worker, exemption, tax relief or state-law result is determined. The current governing test must be applied to the actual relationship.

proposedPublicPatch.title: Separate payroll does not always mean separate employer duties
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Shared workers and different joint-employer tests
proposedPublicPatch.description: The same worker can raise responsibilities for more than one business under the applicable law.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: If businesses share people or employment decisions, separate incorporation and payroll do not by themselves settle responsibility. The wage-law and labour-relations tests must be kept distinct.

sections.heading: A real agency example: hours at two businesses
paragraphs: The Department of Labor’s Opinion Letter FLSA2025-05 considered a restaurant and members club with represented shared operations, managers and workers. On those supplied facts, it concluded the worker’s hours had to be combined and both employers were responsible for compliance with the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), the federal wage-and-hour law.

The letter is limited to the facts supplied and is not a court judgment about every franchise. Its practical lesson is to examine shared hours and real operations, rather than stop at the two payroll names.

sections.heading: An outcome inspection is different from setting a worker’s shift
paragraphs: Identify who selects workers, sets pay and individual schedules, directs performance, disciplines and terminates. A check of the contracted service outcome and an instruction about a named worker’s shift should not both be labelled quality control. Mixed-purpose controls and actual practice matter; neither fact alone completes a legal test.
Franchise classification asks about brand, operating control or assistance and payments. It does not itself decide who has duties to workers.

sections.heading: Which federal law is being applied?
paragraphs: For federal labour-relations law, the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA), the reviewed February 2026 final action restores the 2020 text: the 2023 rule never took effect after court vacatur. Substantial direct and immediate control over one or more listed essential employment terms is central; indirect or unexercised reserved authority has the rule’s qualified supplementary role.

For federal wage-and-hour law (the FLSA), Part 791 is reserved, not a declaration that joint-employer liability disappeared. The Department of Labor’s April 2026 publication is a proposal, not an effective rule or franchise exemption. Governing court law and the actual employment facts remain relevant.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Check shared-worker hours and actual employment decisions before treating two payrolls as two independent wage obligations.
limitations: This makes no joint-employer finding or full governing-court, bargaining-unit or state-law determination. The cited court record is not a complete current docket search.

proposedPublicPatch.title: An import certificate does not close a later safety complaint
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Product certificates and later CPSC reporting duties
proposedPublicPatch.description: Certification and reporting serious new safety information are different responsibilities.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: A certificate concerns the applicable product requirements. New information about a hazard can create a separate reporting question even when a certificate is already on file.

sections.heading: Identify the product and responsible certifier
paragraphs: The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) scope and exclusions depend on the actual article, ordinary users, intended use and other agencies involved. A B2B invoice does not itself remove a product from that inquiry.

For covered imported finished products, Part 1110 defines the importer/certifier role, certificate contents and eFiling. Specified broker, owner, purchaser or consignee allocations are possible, but the identified certifier remains legally responsible for validity, accuracy, completeness and availability. The testing basis must match the actual applicable rules; a bought template is not proof. Keep the certificate and specified supporting records for at least five years from the certificate’s creation date, and meet the separate access and furnishing requirements.

sections.heading: An overheating report needs its own assessment
paragraphs: In a fictional example, a brand receives overheating information after assembling its import certificate file. The old certificate is not a reason to ignore the new facts.

Covered firms can have an immediate reporting duty when information reasonably supports the specified noncompliance, a potentially substantial product hazard or an unreasonable serious-injury/death risk. The rule interprets immediate as 24 hours, with its weekend/holiday computation. Do not wait for a complete risk estimate by default: a reasonable investigation is not automatic permission to delay once reportable information is known. A supplier’s promise to handle it does not settle every other party’s duty.

sections.heading: eFiling policy does not waive safety duties
paragraphs: The final action uses July 8, 2026 for most covered products and January 8, 2027 for specified foreign-trade-zone entries. The reviewed FAQ describes an initial policy against entry denial solely for missing eFiling data while certificate enforcement continues. That time-sensitive policy is not an exemption or guaranteed entry result.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Bring new safety information promptly into the reporting assessment instead of treating the certificate as the end of the issue.
limitations: No product jurisdiction, technical test, reportable-defect, recall or shipment-clearance conclusion is made. The example does not decide whether its complaint is reportable.

sections.heading: Who receives access?
paragraphs: Identify the U.S. person providing access as well as the foreign recipient, data and agreement.
Part 202 can reach reading, viewing, editing or otherwise receiving data through a system or cloud platform. A foreign address alone does not establish a prohibited transaction.

The recorded list names China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela, with China’s stated Hong Kong/Macau scope. sections.heading: The data and count matter
paragraphs: Government-related data has specified regardless-of-volume criteria. Bulk sensitive U.S. personal data uses the following more-than thresholds under the category conditions. paragraphs: Data brokerage and specified human-omic transactions have prohibitions. Relevant vendor, employment and investment transactions can be restricted, subject to actual security and other conditions, including the required diligence programme and annual audit.

The corporate-group administrative/ancillary exemption is bounded. An independent franchise or licence partner is not automatically a subsidiary or affiliate. Prescribed security requirements cannot simply be replaced with controls the business regards as equivalent.

proposedPublicPatch.title: Why a foreign audit may need more work for the FDD
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Foreign audits and FDD accounting requirements
proposedPublicPatch.description: An audit, an acceptable accounting basis and the right reporting companies are three different questions.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: Existing audited accounts can be useful without automatically satisfying Item 21 of the Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD). The U.S. seller, a supporting parent and a subfranchisor can affect which statements are required.

sections.heading: Prepared under which rules, and audited under which standards?
paragraphs: Item 21 specifies U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, or principles permitted by the Securities and Exchange Commission, together with applicable U.S. generally accepted auditing standards. The accounting basis governs preparation; audit standards govern the examination. Having an audit does not answer both.

The current Securities and Exchange Commission general filing rule permits foreign private issuers to use International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), or U.S. GAAP. Other comprehensive accounting principles generally require the specified U.S. GAAP reconciliation, subject to the applicable form. SEC staff guidance distinguishes IASB-issued IFRS from home-country standards and requires the stated compliance in the accounts and auditor’s opinion to omit reconciliation. This establishes the general SEC framework; it does not approve this group’s FDD accounts or replace Item 21’s audit requirements.

sections.heading: Parent support can affect the statement question
paragraphs: In a fictional European group, a new U.S. subsidiary will sell franchises while presentations promise parent training and technical support. Budgeting only for the subsidiary’s opening accounts can miss questions raised by the parent’s obligations or guarantees.

Read the actual commitments. A thin seller does not make parent promises disappear, but a strong parent does not automatically let the seller attach the parent’s annual report instead. Subfranchisor roles raise further requirements.

sections.heading: Allow time for the work actually needed
paragraphs: The required companies and reporting periods, preparation basis, audit approach and any reconciliation affect the cost and delivery date of the FDD. Signing an audit engagement is not completion of that work.

The federal startup phase-in is conditional, not a universal shortcut for an established foreign system or any newly formed U.S. seller. State acceptance and financial-assurance conditions are separate.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Allow for the actual statement and audit work before promising the sales launch date.
limitations: This identifies acceptance issues; it does not determine the exact statements, startup eligibility or state financial conditions for your group.
